title: The pre-commit gate has no cost budget, nothing measures its latency, and it holds the shared index lock for its whole run
body:
The pre-commit gate has no cost budget, nothing declares one, and no instrument measures gate latency. Any guard may add an arbitrarily expensive arm; five concurrent sessions then pay it on every commit, and the only feedback is a human finding the gate slow.

THE INSTANCE THAT PRODUCED THIS, and it is a near-miss rather than a shipped defect. A complement sweep added to `shared_artefact_build_guard.sh` arm 6b read all of `native/rust`, which on this machine is 9.4G of `target/` against 7.8M of `crates`. Measured: the intended walk is 370 files; that draft walked 74,239. It was caught because a verification run hung past a tool timeout and the author went looking -- irritation, not a mechanism. Fixed before landing with `--exclude-dir=target`, declared at the line.

THE SECOND-ORDER COST IS THE ONE NOBODY SEES. The gate holds `.git/index.lock` for its whole run, so its duration is not merely each node's own wait -- it SERIALISES every session on the machine. Observed the same evening: a peer held the lock for 252s while another node's commit waited. A slow arm therefore multiplies by the number of live sessions, and nothing in the estate reports either the duration or the contention.

WHAT IS ALREADY DONE ABOUT IT, so this row is not read as unaddressed. vc ruled 2026-09-04 that the existing denominator IS the cost signal provided it counts the WALK rather than the HITS: `3 examined` says nothing about what was traversed to find 3, and `370 file(s) walked` would have read 74,239 on the bad draft, on the first run, before anything landed. Arm 6b now emits both walk figures unconditionally. That is a smoke detector and it is deployed in exactly one arm.

THE HONEST LIMIT, stated because a proxy presented as a measure is this estate's recurring defect: FILES-WALKED IS NOT COST. A cheap predicate over a million paths can be fine; an expensive one over forty can be ruinous. A real budget needs a latency measurement that does not exist, per-arm and comparable across runs.

WHY THIS IS NOT `AC-00.16`. Reach and cost are different axes even though they wore the same clothes in the founding instance -- the same edit both widened an undeclared reach and made the walk enormous. A criterion about what an instrument covers cannot carry a claim about what it costs, and folding them would mean one green standing for two properties.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: every gated arm reports the population it walked, and something reports the gate's own duration per arm across runs, so that a regression is visible before a human notices the wait.
